readerTitle: Why paying yourself can make your business last longer
caseNote: 가상 사례 (생활용품 소매·도매점, 식당) · 모든 수치는 설명용 · 연구는 일반적 서술로만 인용
insight: 창업자 자신도 런웨이의 일부다. 회사 현금과 창업자의 개인 여력 중 먼저 바닥나는 쪽이 진짜 런웨이다.
misconception: 회복탄력성은 타고난 성격이고, 강한 창업자는 월급도 휴식도 없이 버텨낸다. 자기 급여를 0으로 하면 회사가 더 오래 산다.

sources.text: Sonnentag, S., & Fritz, C. (2007). The Recovery Experience Questionnaire. Journal of Occupational Health Psychology.
Mani, A., Mullainathan, S., Shafir, E., & Zhao, J. (2013). Poverty impedes cognitive function. Science.

factChecks.note: 재정적 압박이 인지 여력을 줄인다는 연구(Mani et al. 2013)는 이후 재현 연구에서 결과가 엇갈렸습니다. 카드에는 "some research suggests"로만 약하게 적고 수치는 인용하지 않았습니다.
업무에서의 심리적 분리(detachment)가 회복에 도움이 된다는 내용은 Sonnentag 등의 회복 연구 흐름을 일반적으로 요약한 것입니다. 카드에 구체 수치나 인과 주장을 넣지 않았는지 다시 확인하세요.

cards.title: The spreadsheet is missing one line.
body: Maya runs a homeware shop that also supplies local cafés. She lost her biggest wholesale customer, and now the business loses $5,000 a month while she rebuilds.
It has $60,000 in the bank. Twelve months of runway, her spreadsheet says. The spreadsheet leaves out one thing: Maya.

image.label: Shop owner looking at a spreadsheet with one blank row
image.brief: 작은 생활용품 가게 카운터에서 주인이 노트북 스프레드시트를 보고 있다. 화면에는 "Cash $60,000", "Runway 12 months" 줄 아래에 비어 있는 한 줄이 강조되어 있음. 따뜻한 일러스트 스타일, 실제 브랜드 로고 없음.

cards.title: How much should Maya pay herself?
body: Maya currently pays herself nothing. Her personal savings are $15,000, and her household costs $3,000 a month.
She wants to give the rebuild as long as possible. Which salary keeps her going longest?

options.text: $0. Every dollar stays in the business
options.feedback: The business lasts 12 months, but her savings run out in 5. That's when she'd be forced to quit or take another job, with 7 months of company cash unused.
The business now lasts about 9 months and her savings about 10. Both tanks empty at roughly the same time, so she gets 9 months instead of 5.

options.text: $3,000 a month, covering her full household costs
options.feedback: Her savings stop falling, which removes a big worry. But the business now loses $8,000 a month and runs dry in 7.5 months.

cards.title: Two tanks, one runway.
body: Her real runway is whichever tank empties first. Paying herself nothing didn't protect the business. It moved the crisis from the shop to her kitchen table, and made it arrive sooner.

cards.title: Founder resilience
body: **Founder resilience** is the capacity to keep making sound decisions through a long, uncertain stretch.
It's often described as a personality trait. In practice, it's closer to a set of reserves you can plan: money, time, people and rest. Maya's savings were one of them, and the smallest.
The shift in view: **you are part of the runway.** Plan your own reserves the way you plan the company's cash.

image.label: Two fuel gauges: business cash and founder reserves
image.brief: 계기판 두 개를 나란히. 왼쪽 "Business cash" 게이지는 거의 가득, 오른쪽 "Founder reserves" 게이지는 빨간 구간 근처. 두 게이지 아래에 하나의 "Runway" 표시가 오른쪽 게이지에 연결되어 있음. 깔끔한 플랫 인포그래픽.

cards.title: Why reserves beat willpower.
body: Willpower runs down. Exhaustion and money worries narrow attention, and some research suggests financial pressure uses up mental capacity people would otherwise spend on planning. A drained founder can cut the wrong costs or put off the hard call.
list: **Money:** a personal floor, even a small salary
**Time:** a fixed day off, and a decision date set in advance
**People:** a peer or mentor who can hear the bad news
**Recovery:** time fully away from the business
cards.callout: Each reserve is cheaper to build before the crisis than during it.
cards.softwareNote: Software founders often calculate runway with their own salary at zero. Run the same two-tank check, and do it for key early employees too. Their personal runway can end the company's plans just as fast.

cards.title: Resilience is not the same as never quitting.
body: Reserves buy time to decide well. They are not a reason to avoid deciding. If the numbers keep saying no, the resilient move may be to change direction or close the business cleanly.
Reserves also cost something. Maya's salary shortened the business's runway from 12 months to about 9. The goal is balance between the tanks, not comfort at the company's expense.

cards.title: Now it's a restaurant.
body: Dev owns a 40-seat restaurant rebuilding after a bad year. He works every shift, seven days a week, to save on staff.
Three months in, he's making small mistakes on orders and has delayed a menu decision for weeks. What should he do?

image.label: Tired restaurant owner at the pass late at night
image.brief: 늦은 밤 식당 주방 패스 앞에서 지친 주인이 주문서 더미를 보고 있다. 벽 달력에 7일 모두 X 표시. 차분한 색감 일러스트, 실제 상호나 로고 없음.

options.text: Keep going. Cutting costs matters most right now
options.feedback: It saves wages but spends his scarcest resource, his judgment. Order mistakes and a stalled menu decision cost money too.

options.text: Hire a shift lead for two quiet nights, take one day fully off, and block a morning for the menu decision
options.feedback: It costs some wages, like Maya's salary, but buys back rest and thinking time. One tank gets a little shorter so the other doesn't run dry.

options.text: Close two days a week so he can rest
options.feedback: It protects his energy but gives up revenue. Worth it only if those days lose money anyway.

cards.title: You are part of the runway.
body: A business lasts only as long as its cash and its founder. Plan both, and build your reserves before you need them.
**Try it today:** write two numbers. How many months your business can run on its cash, and how many months you can personally keep going. Which one is shorter?
